title: 不要 + verb: don't
summary: Lets you tell someone not to do something, as in 不要说话.
explanation:
不要 + verb tells someone NOT to do something: 不要说话 'Don't talk.' Add 请 to be polite: 请不要在这里打电话 'Please don't make calls here.' You can put 你 or 你们 first to make it clear who you mean.

不要 + a thing simply means 'don't want': 我不要这个 'I don't want this one.' For 'don't want to do', use 不想 instead.

examples.en: Please don't make phone calls here.
Don't drink tea in the evening.
I don't want this one; I want that one.

mistakes.why: 不要 goes before the verb.
'Don't' is 不要, not 没要.

exercises.instruction: Tell someone NOT to do it.
why: Correct: 不要 before the verb.
不要 can't go at the end.
This mixes 没 and 不要 in the wrong places.

exercises.prompt: A polite sign in a library says:
why: 不要 goes before the verb.

exercises.why: 请 first, then 不要, then the verb.

exercises.prompt: Which means 'I don't want to go'?
why: Correct: 'don't want to' is 不想.
不要去 tells someone not to go; adding 吧 doesn't fix that.
没要 isn't used like this.

exercises.en: Don't play with your phone in class.
why: Correct: 不要 = 'don't' as an order.
不 alone describes a habit; it doesn't tell someone not to.
